subject.title: [Feature]: Thread replies when agent uses tools; top-level for conversational responses

question: Should Slack add a default-off tool-use-sensitive reply policy, and what precedence should it have relative to replyToMode, per-channel overrides, DMs/group DMs, existing threads, explicit top-level opt-outs, streaming previews, and status indicators?
rationale: The source-level feature absence is clear, but the requested solution adds compatibility-sensitive Slack config and message placement behavior that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Approve a precise Slack policy
options.body: Define the config shape and precedence, then implement the Slack-owned schema, routing, docs, and tests with default false for existing installs.

options.title: Use static reply controls only
options.body: Treat account, chat-type, and per-channel replyToMode as the supported Slack channel-cleanliness controls and close this feature as not planned.

options.title: Defer to cross-channel design
options.body: Hold this issue until maintainers define a broader reply-placement policy that can cover Slack without one-off config drift.

recommendation.title: Approve a precise Slack policy
recommendation.body: Define the config shape and precedence, then implement the Slack-owned schema, routing, docs, and tests with default false for existing installs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history signal on adjacent Slack thread-safety and reply-mode behavior.
